# Summary

This notebook cleans the mortality data from the 1630-1631 Venetian Plague, calculates the Shannon entropy and negentropy of the quantile function and the PDF, and uses bootstrapping to find 95% confidence intervals.

# Data Cleaning

Now, we perform preliminary cleaning.

```{r first_pass_cleaning}

all$Date <- sub("2029", "1629", all$Date)
all$Date <- sub("2030", "1630", all$Date)
all$Date <- sub("2031", "1631", all$Date)
all$Date <- as.Date(all$Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")

# Fix artifacts for column names
colnames(all) <- sub("^S\\.", "S", colnames(all))

# Remove diacritics
colnames(all) <- stri_trans_general(colnames(all), id = "Latin-ASCII")
```

Clean the population datasets.

```{r population_cleaning}
colnames(population_pre) <- c("Parish", "Population_1509", "Population_1551", 
                              "Population_1581", "Population_1586")

# Remove space artifacts
population_pre$Parish <- gsub("[[:space:]]", ".", population_pre$Parish)
population_pre$Parish <- sub("^S\\.", "S", population_pre$Parish)

# Remove diacritics
population_pre$Parish <- stri_trans_general(population_pre$Parish, id = "Latin-ASCII")

# Remove space artifacts
population_post$Parish <- gsub("[[:space:]]", ".", population_post$Parish)
population_post$Parish <- sub("^S\\.", "S", population_post$Parish)

# Remove diacritics
population_post$Parish <- stri_trans_general(population_post$Parish, id = "Latin-ASCII")

# Identify and remove the parishes that are not contained in both the 
# 1586 census and the 1696 census
remove_vec <- c()
for(i in 1:length(population_pre$Parish)){
  if(!(population_pre$Parish[i] %in% population_post$Parish)){
    remove_vec <- c(remove_vec,i)
  }
}

if(length(remove_vec) > 0){
  population_pre <- population_pre[-remove_vec,]
}

remove_vec <- c()
for(i in 1:length(population_post$Parish)){
  if(!(population_post$Parish[i] %in% population_pre$Parish)){
    remove_vec <- c(remove_vec, i)
  }
}

if(length(remove_vec) > 0){
  population_post <- population_post[-remove_vec,]
}

# Establish a consistent ordering of the parishes (alphabetical)
population_post <- population_post %>% arrange(Parish)
population_pre <- population_pre %>% arrange(Parish)

# Remove the 1509 census data because the vast majority of values are NAs
population_pre <- population_pre[,-2]

# In the population_pre dataset, the thousands place is marked by a period. 
# Unfortunately, R interprets these as decimal points. Because parishes with 
# populations smaller than 1000 are unaffected by this, we use the format
# function with 3 decimal places to exclude parishes with populations smaller than 1000.
# Specifically, these parishes all have populations with 3 digits, so adding
# the decimal point and three zeroes will result in their population numbers
# having 7 characters.
# All of the population numbers greater than 1000 are also less than 100,000, 
# so the 7 character rule never accidentally excludes the wrong parishes.
# Additionally, using the format function with three decimal places ensures that
# trailing zeroes are accounted for.
# Thus, we only scale the numbers that have less than 7 characters.

for(j in 1:ncol(population_pre)){
  if(j == 1){
    next
  }
  for(i in 1:nrow(population_pre)){
    population_pre[i,j] <- format(as.numeric(population_pre[i,j]), nsmall = 3)
    
    if(nchar(population_pre[i,j]) < 7){ 
      population_pre[i,j] <- as.numeric(population_pre[i,j]) * 1000
    } else {
      population_pre[i,j] <- as.numeric(population_pre[i,j])
    }
  }
  population_pre[,j] <- as.numeric(population_pre[,j])
}
population_post$Population <- as.numeric(population_post$Population) * 1000

# Merge population_pre and population_post into one dataframe, population_df
population_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(population_pre, population_post[,-1]))
colnames(population_df) <- c("Parish", "Population_1551", "Population_1581", 
                             "Population_1586", "Population_1696")

# Plot the population data over time
year_vec <- c(c(1551, 1581, 1586, 1696))

t_pop_df <- transpose(population_df)
rownames(t_pop_df) <- colnames(population_df)
t_pop_df <- t_pop_df[-1,]
colnames(t_pop_df) <- population_df$Parish
t_pop_df <- cbind(year_vec, t_pop_df)
t_pop_df_plot <- t_pop_df %>% 
  gather(key = "Parish_var", value = "value", -year_vec)
t_pop_df_plot$value <- as.numeric(t_pop_df_plot$value)

t_pop_df_plot %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year_vec, y = value))+
  geom_line(aes(color = Parish_var), show.legend = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5)+
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Population", 
       title = "Population over Time for each Parish")+
  scale_y_log10()+
  theme_minimal()
```

Run a linear regression on the Venetian census data from 1696 vs. 1586 to determine the validity of using linear interpolation to estimate 1629 parish populations.

```{r linear_regression}
cor(population_df$Population_1586, population_df$Population_1696) #0.95

plot(x = population_df$Population_1586, y = population_df$Population_1696)

abline(mod <- lm(population_df$Population_1696 ~ population_df$Population_1586)) 
# y = 1696, x = 1586 (closest census date) so slope < 1 means that 
# population decreased over time

intercept <- as.numeric(coef(mod)[1])
slope <- as.numeric(coef(mod)[2]) #slope, close to 1 so we feel comfortable interpolating
```

Due to the high $r$ value (0.95) and the slope being close to 1, we feel comfortable linearly interpolating between the 1696 and 1586 population data to estimate each parish's population on January 1, 1629.

```{r interpolation}
# Per-parish interpolation
interpolated_1629 <- as.numeric(population_df$Population_1586) + (43 / 110) * (population_df$Population_1696 - population_df$Population_1586)

# Population-wide interpolation using linear regression results
# 1629 - 1586 = 43, 1696 - 1586 = 110, so to interpolate we multiply by 43/110
#interpolated_1629 <- (intercept - (1-slope) * population_pre$Population_1586) * 43/110 + population_pre$Population_1586
```

Finally, we figure out which parishes we will keep. The code below removes San Marco from our analysis because it served as a placeholder for deaths from drowning and those in prison, which resulted in an early spike in cases not representative of parish transmission. In our main analysis, we exclude it, but in the supplementary information, we include San Marco as a form of sensitivity analysis. The other two parishes we exclude are those which had no data during the primary outbreak window (9/1/30-12/31/30). 

```{r outlier_handling}
outliers <- c("S.Polo", "S.Stae", "S.Marco") #No cases between 9/1/30 and 12/31/30, outbreak time
filled_modified <- filled[, !(colnames(filled) %in% outliers)]
sestiere_df_modified <- sestiere_df[!(sestiere_df$Parish %in% outliers),]
population_specified_modified <- population_specified[!(population_specified$Parish %in% outliers),]
```

# Define Statistic-Calculating Functions

In this section, we define the functions that calculate the statistics of interest (entropy and KL divergence of the quantile function and PDF).

## Define PDF Approximation Function

For our histogram approximation of the PDF, we use Sturges's Rule to choose $K$, the number of bins, for $N$ observations ($K = \log_2(N)+1$).

```{r define_PDF_approx}
#Define a function that provides a histogram approximation of a PDF with K bins. Here, we use Sturges's Rule for K.
PDF_approx <- function(x, K = ceiling(log2(length(x))) + 1) {
  p <- table(cut(x, breaks = K)) / length(x)
  return(p)
}
```

## Define Kullback-Leibler Divergence

To calculate Kullback-Leibler divergence between two discrete probability distributions P(x) and Q(x), we use the definition $\sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} P(x) \log \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}$. While this formulation implies that KL divergence is undefined when $P(x) = Q(x) = 0$, we [consider the contribution of the KL divergence at that point to be zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kullback%E2%80%93Leibler_divergence#Definition).

To see how this function compares with other methods of calculating Kullback-Leibler Divergence, see [this section](#compare-negentropy-calculations).

```{r define_KL}
#Next, we define Kullback-Leibler divergence between two discrete probability distributions (x and y), formatted as vectors. We add a small value epsilon to avoid dividing by zero.
KL_new <- function(x, y, epsilon = 1e-05){
  distance = 0
  pq_ratio = 0
  if(length(x) != length(y)){
    print("not same length")
    return(NA)
  }
  for(i in 1:length(x)){
    if(is.nan(x[i]) | is.nan(y[i]) | x[i] == 0){
      next
    }
    if(y[i] == 0){
      pq_ratio = x[i] / epsilon
    } else {
      pq_ratio = x[i] / y[i]
    }
    distance = distance + x[i] * log(pq_ratio)
  }
  return(distance)
}
```

For a discrete probability distribution $P(x)$ taking values in the set $\mathcal{X}$, we define the Shannon entropy $H$ to be $H = -\sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} P(x) \ln P(x)$. This definition is implemented directly in the main analysis function. 

## Find the Entropy of the Gaussian Distribution with Identical Mean and Variance to the Data
```{r find normal distribution entropy}
#----
#' Documentation: normal_approx
#' Usage: normal_approx(x, K)
#' @description: Takes in a vector of mortality at a given time point and generates a histogram approximation of a Gaussian distribution with identical mean and variance to the data using midpoint density estimation

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param x: a vector containing the mortality rates of each parish at a specific point in time
#' @param K: the number of bins to use (DEFAULT: ceiling(log2(length(x))) + 1), Sturges' Rule)

#' @return: a vector of length K containing the densities in each bin of the normal distribution as described above
#----

normal_approx <- function (x, K = ceiling(log2(length(x))) + 1){
  bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = K + 1)
  bins2 <- rep(0, K)
  for(i in 1:K){
    bins2[i] <- (bins[i] + bins[i + 1]) / 2
  }
  y <- dnorm(bins2, mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x)) # Midpoint density estimation
  y <- y / sum(y)
  return(y)
}

#----
#' Documentation: calculate_normal_entropy
#' Usage: calculate_normal_entropy(death_data, population_data, cumulative)
#' @description: Takes in death and population data and outputs a vector containing the entropy of the histogram-approximated normal distribution (using Sturges' Rule) with the same mean and variance as the data on each day.

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param death_data: a dataframe containing parishes as columns, days as rows, and death counts as entries. The first column is excluded (typically because it contains date data).
#' @param population_data: 
#' @param cumulative: a boolean specifying whether all deaths up to each time point are included (TRUE) or if only the deaths on that day are included (FALSE). (DEFAULT: TRUE)

#' @return: a vector of length nrow(death_data) containing the entropy of the histrogram-approximated normal distribution with the same mean and variance as the data on each day in the epidemic.
#----

calculate_normal_entropy <- function(death_data, population_data, cumulative = TRUE){
  max_entropy_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(death_data))
  for(i in 1:nrow(death_data)){
    if(cumulative){
      case_vector <- colSums(death_data[1:i,-1]) / (population_data$Population * 1000)
    } else {
      case_vector <- as.numeric(death_data[i, -1]) / (population_data$Population * 1000)
    }
    p <- normal_approx(case_vector)
    max_entropy <- -1 * sum(p * log(p))
    max_entropy_vec[i] <- max_entropy
  }
  return(max_entropy_vec)
}
```

## Define Main Analaysis Function

Now, we define our main analysis function which returns the total number of deaths, Shannon entropy of the PDF, Shannon Entropy of the quantile function, negentropy of the PDF (KL divergence with a Gaussian), KL divergence of the PDF from a uniform, and KL divergence of the quantile from a discrete uniform at a given timestep. Later, we will run this function on the 999 resampled datasets generated during the bootstrapping process.

```{r define_entropy_procedure}
#---- 
#' Documentation: entropy_procedure
#' Usage: entropy_procedure(original_data, subset, indices, timestep, cumulative)
#' @description: Return a list containing the sum of all cases (sum), 
#' Shannon entropy of the PDF (shannonPDF), 
#' Shannon entropy of the quantile function (shannonQuantile), 
#' KL divergence of the PDF from a Gaussian distribution (negentPDF), 
#' KL divergence of the PDF from a uniform distribution (uniformKL_PDF),
#' and KL divergence of the quantile function from a uniform distribution (uniformKL_Quantile)
#' calculated on mortality data in a specified subset of parishes on or up to a particular day

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param original_data: a dataframe containing one variable for every parish of interest. Note that original_data does NOT get modified by subset, so original_data must already be subsetted if one only wishes to include a smaller selection of parishes.
#' @param subset: a vector containing the indices of the parishes of interest in colnames(filled_modified).
#' @param indices: a vector containing the indices generated by sampling with replacement. To analyze the original data, set indices = 1:ncol(original_data).
#' @param timestep: an integer between 1 and nrow(filled_modified) corresponding to the day for which the aforementioned statistics should be calculated.
#' @param cumulative: a boolean specifying whether deaths occurring on days prior to timestep should be included. If cumulative is set to FALSE, only deaths on day "timestep" will be considered. If cumulative is set to TRUE, deaths up to and including day "timestep" will be added up (DEFAULT: TRUE)

#' @return: the list as described above
#----

entropy_procedure <- function(original_data,
           subset,
           indices,
           timestep,
           cumulative = TRUE) {
    boot_data <- original_data[, indices]
    # The proper index for pop_spec is subset - 1 because filled has a "Date"
    # column while population_specified_modified does not
    pop_spec <- population_specified_modified[subset - 1, ][indices, ]
    if (cumulative) {
      non_pop_corrected <- as.numeric(colSums(boot_data[1:timestep, ]))
    } else {
      non_pop_corrected <- as.numeric(boot_data[timestep, ])
    }
    
    # Case vector (cv): cases in each parish divided by parish population
    cv <- non_pop_corrected / (pop_spec$Population * 1000)
    cv <- sort(cv)
    
    # Normalized case vector (cv_norm): quantile function
    cv_norm <- cv / sum(cv)
    
    # Kernel (kern): histogram of mortality with # bins specified by Sturges's Rule
    kern <- as.numeric(PDF_approx(cv))
    
    kern <- kern / sum(kern)
    
    shannon_PDF <- -1 * sum(kern[kern != 0] * log(kern[kern != 0]))
    shannon_quantile <-
      -1 * sum(cv_norm[cv_norm != 0] * log(cv_norm[cv_norm != 0]))
    
    # Use the msos negent function to calculate the negentropy of the PDF
    negent_PDF <- negent(cv) 

    uniform_KL_PDF <-
      as.numeric(KL_new(kern, rep(1 / length(kern), length(kern))))
    uniform_KL_quantile <-
      KL_new(cv_norm, rep(1 / length(cv_norm), length(cv_norm)))
    return(
      list(
        sum = sum(non_pop_corrected) / (sum(pop_spec$Population) * 1000),
        shannonPDF = shannon_PDF,
        shannonQuantile = shannon_quantile,
        negentPDF = negent_PDF,
        uniformKL_PDF = uniform_KL_PDF,
        uniformKL_Quantile = uniform_KL_quantile
      )
    )
  }
```

# Bootstrapping

In this section of code, we run bootstrapping (*n* = 999) to identify 95% confidence intervals for all of the statistics we calculate.

## Define Bootstrapping Functions

Now, we implement a generalized function to bootstrap over our entropy_procedure function. We will utilize this function in the subsequent functions bootstrapping over a particular dataset.

```{r define manual_boot_modified}
#----
#' Documentation: manual_boot_modified
#' Usage: manual_boot_modified(data, subset, N, max_ts, cumulative)
#' @description: Returns a list containing six matrices formatted with dates as columns and resamples as rows. In order, the matrices contain: 
#' the sum of all cases (sum_mat), 
#' Shannon entropy of the PDF (shannonPDF_mat), 
#' Shannon entropy of the quantile function (shannonQuantile_mat), 
#' KL divergence of the PDF from a Gaussian distribution (negentPDF_mat), 
#' KL divergence of the PDF from a uniform distribution (uniformKL_PDF_mat),
#' and KL divergence of the quantile function from a uniform distribution (uniformKL_Quantile_mat)
#' calculated on mortality data in a specified subset of parishes on or up to a particular day.

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param data: a dataframe containing one variable for every parish of interest. Note that data does NOT get modified by the parameter "subset", so data must already be subsetted if one only wishes to include a smaller selection of parishes.
#' @param subset: a vector containing the indices of the parishes of interest in colnames(filled_modified).
#' @param N: an integer denoting the number of resamples to perform.
#' @param max_ts: an integer corresponding to the final day for which the aforementioned statistics should be calculated.
#' @param cumulative: a boolean specifying whether deaths occurring on days prior to timestep should be included. If cumulative is set to FALSE, the aforementioned calculations for a given day will only consider the deaths on that given day. If cumulative is set to TRUE, deaths up to and including that day will be summed.

# @return: the list as described above
#----

manual_boot_modified <- function(
    data,
    subset,
    N,
    max_ts,
    cumulative,
    cores = 7L,
    seed = 123
) {
  metric_names <- c(
    "sum",
    "shannonPDF",
    "shannonQuantile",
    "negentPDF",
    "uniformKL_PDF",
    "uniformKL_Quantile"
  )

  N <- as.integer(N)
  max_ts <- as.integer(max_ts)
  cores <- as.integer(cores)

  stopifnot(
    N >= 1L,
    max_ts >= 1L,
    cores >= 1L
  )

  n_samples <- ncol(data)

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  bootstrap_once <- function(i) {
    sample_index <- sample.int(
      n = n_samples,
      size = n_samples,
      replace = TRUE
    )

    result_matrix <- vapply(
      seq_len(max_ts),
      FUN = function(t) {
        result <- entropy_procedure(
          data,
          subset,
          sample_index,
          t,
          cumulative
        )

        values <- c(
          sum = result$sum,
          shannonPDF = result$shannonPDF,
          shannonQuantile = result$shannonQuantile,
          negentPDF = result$negentPDF,
          uniformKL_PDF = result$uniformKL_PDF,
          uniformKL_Quantile = result$uniformKL_Quantile
        )

        if (length(values) != length(metric_names)) {
          stop(
            "entropy_procedure() did not return exactly one value ",
            "for each of the six metrics at t = ",
            t,
            "."
          )
        }

        if (!is.numeric(values)) {
          stop(
            "entropy_procedure() returned nonnumeric values at t = ",
            t,
            "."
          )
        }

        as.numeric(values)
      },
      FUN.VALUE = numeric(length(metric_names)),
      USE.NAMES = FALSE
    )

    rownames(result_matrix) <- metric_names
    storage.mode(result_matrix) <- "double"

    result_matrix
  }

  bootstrap_indices <- seq_len(N)

  if (cores > 1L && .Platform$OS.type != "windows") {
    bootstrap_results <- parallel::mclapply(
      bootstrap_indices,
      bootstrap_once,
      mc.cores = min(cores, N),
      mc.preschedule = TRUE,
      mc.set.seed = TRUE
    )
  } else {
    if (cores > 1L && .Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
      warning(
        "Fork-based parallelization is unavailable on Windows; ",
        "running sequentially."
      )
    }

    bootstrap_results <- lapply(
      bootstrap_indices,
      bootstrap_once
    )
  }

  output <- setNames(
    lapply(
      seq_along(metric_names),
      function(metric_index) {
        # Result before transposition: max_ts × N
        metric_matrix <- vapply(
          bootstrap_results,
          FUN = function(result) {
            as.numeric(result[metric_index, ])
          },
          FUN.VALUE = numeric(max_ts),
          USE.NAMES = FALSE
        )

        # Preserve original output dimensions: N × max_ts
        metric_matrix <- t(metric_matrix)
        storage.mode(metric_matrix) <- "double"

        metric_matrix
      }
    ),
    metric_names
  )

  valid_output <- vapply(
    output,
    FUN = function(x) {
      is.matrix(x) &&
        is.numeric(x) &&
        identical(dim(x), c(N, max_ts))
    },
    FUN.VALUE = logical(1)
  )

  if (!all(valid_output)) {
    stop(
      "Invalid bootstrap output for: ",
      paste(names(valid_output)[!valid_output], collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  output
}
```

## Identify 95% CI

In our main analysis, we find the 97.5th and 2.5th percentile values at each time point (accomplished by simply sorting for each day and indexing for the desired percentile, a task which is already performed in the bootstrapping functions themselves). However, as a sensitivity analysis, we define a function here which sums up the values across each run and approximates the 97.5th and 2.5th percentile full runs. 

```{r define find_closest_run}
#----
#' Documentation: find_closest_run
#' Usage: find_closest_run(all_runs, target_percentile)
#' @description: Returns in vector form the row of a specified dataframe with the nth lowest sum (n = target_percentile)

#' Arguments/Options: 
#' @param all_runs: a dataframe containing numeric values with one column for every time point and one row for every resampling
#' @param target_percentile: an integer describing the index of the desired sorted vector all_runs. For example, if all_runs contains 1000 rows, the 97.5th percentile row selected by setting target_percentile = 975)

#' @return: the numeric vector as described above
#----

find_closest_run <- function(all_runs, target_percentile) {
  all_runs_sum <- rowSums(all_runs)
  sorted_all_runs_sum <- sort(all_runs_sum)
  index <- match(sorted_all_runs_sum[target_percentile], all_runs_sum)
  return(as.numeric(all_runs[index,]))
}
```

## Per-sestiere analysis

Now, we define the analysis and bootstrapping functions for the per-sestiere analysis.

```{r define_sestiere_bootstrapping}
#----
#' Documentation: shannonBySestiere
#' Usage: shannonBySestiere(cumulative)
#' @description: Returns a list of 6 lists (one for each sestiere). Each list contains six numerical vectors (one for each statistic) with entries for every day in the epidemic. 

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param cumulative: a boolean specifying whether deaths occurring on days prior to timestep should be included. If cumulative is set to FALSE, the aforementioned calculations for a given day will only consider the deaths on that given day. If cumulative is set to TRUE, deaths up to and including that day will be summed (DEFAULT: TRUE)

#' @return: the list as described above
#----
shannonBySestiere <- function(cumulative = TRUE) {
  # Initialize vectors
  sum_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date))
  shannonPDF_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date))
  shannonQuantile_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date))
  negentPDF_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date))
  uniformKL_PDF_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date))
  uniformKL_Quantile_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date))
  
  # Initialize the output list
  all_runs_list <-
    vector(mode = "list", length = length(unique(sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere)))
  
  for (s in unique(sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere)) {
    # Generate a vector containing the indices of the current sestiere's parishes
    sestiere_parishes <-
      match(sestiere_df_modified$Parish[sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere == s], colnames(filled_modified))
    for (i in 1:length(filled_modified$Date)) {
      current_list <-
        entropy_procedure(
          filled_modified[, sestiere_parishes], # Subset the data using sestiere_parishes
          subset = sestiere_parishes,
          seq(
            1,
            length(sestiere_parishes),
            length.out = length(sestiere_parishes)
          ),
          timestep = i,
          cumulative = cumulative
        )
      sum_vec[i] <- current_list$sum
      shannonPDF_vec[i] <- current_list$shannonPDF
      shannonQuantile_vec[i] <- current_list$shannonQuantile
      negentPDF_vec[i] <- current_list$negentPDF
      uniformKL_PDF_vec[i] <- current_list$uniformKL_PDF
      uniformKL_Quantile_vec[i] <- current_list$uniformKL_Quantile
    }
    # For each sestiere, store a list of the six statistic vectors in all_runs_list
    all_runs_list[[match(s, unique(sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere))]] <-
      list(
        sum = sum_vec,
        shannonPDF = shannonPDF_vec,
        shannonQuantile = shannonQuantile_vec,
        negentPDF = negentPDF_vec,
        uniformKL_PDF = uniformKL_PDF_vec,
        uniformKL_Quantile = uniformKL_Quantile_vec
      )
  }
  return(all_runs_list)
}

#----
#' Documentation: shannonBySestiere_Bootstrapped
#' Usage: shannonBySestiere_Bootstrapped(cumulative)
#' @description: Returns a list containing 6 lists (one for each sestiere), each containing 5 matrices formatted with each statistic as a column and each day as a row. In order, the matrices contain: 
#' the 5th percentile value of each statistic calculated separately on each day (b1), 
#' the 95th percentile value of each statistic calculated separately on each day (b2), 
#' the value of the 5th percentile resample for each statistic (closest_runs_025), 
#' the value of the 5th percentile resample for each statistic (closest_runs_975), 
#' calculated on mortality data in each sestiere on or up to a particular day.

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param cumulative: a boolean specifying whether deaths occurring on days prior to timestep should be included. If cumulative is set to FALSE, the aforementioned calculations for a given day will only consider the deaths on that given day. If cumulative is set to TRUE, deaths up to and including that day will be summed (DEFAULT: TRUE)

#' @return: the list as described above
#----

shannonBySestiere_Bootstrapped <- function(cumulative = TRUE) {
  num_dates <- length(filled_modified$Date)
  sestiere_list <- unique(sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere)
  num_sestieri <- length(sestiere_list)
  
  # Keep track of run time
  st <- Sys.time()
  
  # Initialize all_runs_list, which we will eventually return
  all_runs_list <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(sestiere_list))
  
  for (s in sestiere_list) {
    cat("Processing:", s, "\n")
    s_index <- match(s, sestiere_list)
    
    # Find the indices of the parishes in sestiere "s" in filled_modified
    sestiere_parishes <- match(sestiere_df_modified$Parish[sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere == s], colnames(filled_modified))
    
    # Subset the mortality data to only consider the parishes in sestiere "s"
    data_subset <- filled_modified[, sestiere_parishes]
    
    boot_mat <- manual_boot_modified(data = data_subset, 
                                       subset = sestiere_parishes, N = 999, 
                                       max_ts = num_dates, 
                                       cumulative = cumulative)
    
    #Initialize the upper and lower bound matrices
    b1_mat <- matrix(NA, ncol = length(boot_mat), nrow = num_dates)
    b2_mat <- matrix(NA, ncol = length(boot_mat), nrow = num_dates)
    
    closest_runs_025_mat <- matrix(NA, ncol = length(boot_mat), nrow = num_dates)
    closest_runs_975_mat <- matrix(NA,ncol = length(boot_mat), nrow = num_dates)
    #b1[, s_index] <- apply(boot_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
    #b2[, s_index] <- apply(boot_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
    for(j in 1:length(boot_mat)){
      closest_runs_025_mat[,j] <- find_closest_run(boot_mat[[j]], 25)
      closest_runs_975_mat[,j] <- find_closest_run(boot_mat[[j]], 975)
      for(i in 1:ncol(boot_mat[[j]])){
        sorted <- sort(as.numeric(boot_mat[[j]][,i]))
        b1_mat[i, j] <- sorted[25]
        b2_mat[i, j] <- sorted[975]
      }
    }
    all_runs_list[[match(s,sestiere_list)]] <- list(b1 = b1_mat, b2 = b2_mat, closest_runs_025 = closest_runs_025_mat, closest_runs_975 = closest_runs_975_mat)
  }
  ed <- Sys.time()
  print(ed - st)
  return(all_runs_list)
}
```

## Whole Dataset Analysis

Finally, we define the functions for the bootstrapping of the whole dataset.

```{r define_whole_dataset_analysis}
#----
#' Documentation: whole_dataset_analysis
#' Usage: whole_dataset_analysis(cumulative)
#' @description: Returns a list of 6 vectors, each containing the value of a particular statistic for every day in the epidemic.

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param cumulative: a boolean specifying whether deaths occurring on days prior to timestep should be included. If cumulative is set to FALSE, the aforementioned calculations for a given day will only consider the deaths on that given day. If cumulative is set to TRUE, deaths up to and including that day will be summed (DEFAULT: TRUE)

#' @return: the list as described above
#----
whole_dataset_analysis <- function(cumulative = TRUE){
  # Initialize the vectors for each statistic
  sum_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date)) # cumulative deaths
  shannonPDF_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date)) # Shannon entropy of the PDF
  shannonQuantile_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date)) # Shannon entropy of the quantile function
  negentPDF_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date)) # KL divergence of the PDF from a Gaussian
  uniformKL_PDF_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date)) # KL divergence of the PDF from a uniform
  uniformKL_Quantile_vec <- rep(0, length(filled_modified$Date)) # KL divergence of the quantile function from a uniform
  
  st <- Sys.time() # Record the starting time
  pb <- progress_bar$new(total = length(filled_modified$Date)) # Create a progress bar
  
  for(i in 1:length(filled_modified$Date)){
    current_list <- entropy_procedure(filled_modified[,-1], subset = 2:ncol(filled_modified), indices = 1:ncol(filled_modified[,-1]), timestep = i, cumulative)
    sum_vec[i] <- current_list$sum
    shannonPDF_vec[i] <- current_list$shannonPDF
    shannonQuantile_vec[i] <- current_list$shannonQuantile
    negentPDF_vec[i] <- current_list$negentPDF
    uniformKL_PDF_vec[i] <- current_list$uniformKL_PDF
    uniformKL_Quantile_vec[i] <- current_list$uniformKL_Quantile
    pb$tick()
  }
  ed <- Sys.time() # Record the final time
  print(ed - st) # Print the runtime
  return(list(sum = sum_vec, shannonPDF = shannonPDF_vec, shannonQuantile = shannonQuantile_vec, negentPDF = negentPDF_vec, uniformKL_PDF = uniformKL_PDF_vec, uniformKL_Quantile = uniformKL_Quantile_vec))
}

#----
#' Documentation: whole_dataset_bootstrap
#' Usage: whole_dataset_bootstrap(cumulative)
#' @description: Returns a list of 4 lists. Lists b1 and b2 correspond to the 2.5th and 97.5th percentile values at every time step, respectively, while lists closest_run_025 and closest_runs_975 correspond to the values of the 2.5th and 97.5th percentile trials, respectively. 

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param cumulative: a boolean specifying whether deaths occurring on days prior to timestep should be included. If cumulative is set to FALSE, the aforementioned calculations for a given day will only consider the deaths on that given day. If cumulative is set to TRUE, deaths up to and including that day will be summed (DEFAULT: TRUE)

#' @return: the list as described above
#----
whole_dataset_bootstrap <- function(cumulative = TRUE){
  num_dates <- length(filled_modified$Date)
  b1 <- rep(0, num_dates) # 2.5%
  b2 <- rep(0, num_dates) # 97.5%
  boot_mat <- manual_boot_modified(data = filled_modified[,-1], subset = 2:ncol(filled_modified), N = 999, max_ts = num_dates, cumulative = cumulative)
  b1_list <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(boot_mat))
  b2_list <- vector(mode = "list",length = length(boot_mat))
  closest_runs_025_list <- vector(mode = "list", length(boot_mat))
  closest_runs_975_list <- vector(mode = "list", length(boot_mat))
    #b1[, s_index] <- apply(boot_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
    #b2[, s_index] <- apply(boot_mat, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  for(j in 1:length(boot_mat)){
    closest_025 <- find_closest_run(boot_mat[[j]], 25)
    closest_975 <- find_closest_run(boot_mat[[j]], 975)
    for(i in 1:ncol(boot_mat[[j]])){
      sorted <- sort(as.numeric(boot_mat[[j]][,i]))
      b1[i] <- sorted[25]
      b2[i] <- sorted[975]
    }
    b1_list[[j]] <- b1
    b2_list[[j]] <- b2
    closest_runs_025_list[[j]] <- closest_025
    closest_runs_975_list[[j]] <- closest_975
  }
  return(list(b1 = b1_list, b2 = b2_list, closest_runs_025 = closest_runs_025_list, closest_runs_975 = closest_runs_975_list))
}
```

## Effective Number of Parishes

Next, we validate our results against the effective number of parties $\left(\frac{1}{\sum_{i}^{n}p_i^2}\right)$, which has a more direct interpretation.

```{r effective number}
#Effective number and log of non-zeroes
non_zeroes_cumulative <- rep(0,length(filled$Date))
eff_number_cumulative <- rep(0,length(filled$Date))
non_zeroes_instantaneous <- rep(0,length(filled$Date))
eff_number_instantaneous <- rep(0,length(filled$Date))

for(i in 1:length(filled$Date)){
  case_vec_cumulative <- as.numeric(colSums(filled_modified[1:i,-1]))/(population_specified_modified$Population*1000)
  case_vec_cumulative_norm <- case_vec_cumulative/sum(case_vec_cumulative)
  case_vec_instantaneous <- as.numeric(filled_modified[i,-1])/(population_specified_modified$Population*1000)
  case_vec_instantaneous_norm <- case_vec_instantaneous/sum(case_vec_instantaneous)
  case_vec_cumulative_norm_nonzeroes <- case_vec_cumulative_norm[case_vec_cumulative_norm != 0]
  non_zeroes_cumulative[i] <- length(case_vec_cumulative_norm_nonzeroes)
  eff_number_cumulative[i] <- 1/sum(case_vec_cumulative_norm_nonzeroes^2)
  case_vec_instantaneous_norm_nonzeroes <- case_vec_instantaneous_norm[case_vec_instantaneous_norm != 0]
  non_zeroes_instantaneous[i] <- length(case_vec_instantaneous_norm_nonzeroes)
  eff_number_instantaneous[i] <- 1/sum(case_vec_instantaneous_norm_nonzeroes^2)
}

# Inverse Simpson's Index is Diversity with q = 2 while the Shannon Index is Diversity with q = 1
# plot.ts(log(non_zeroes_cumulative),ylim=c(2,4),col="red")

```

# Figures

Finally, we plot our results!

## Figure 2

First, we create Figure 2, a grid plot consisting of:

1.  Shannon entropy of the quantile function of cumulative mortality for every day in the epidemic along with corresponding 95% confidence intervals
2.  KL divergence of the quantile function of cumulative mortality from a uniform distribution for every day in the epidemic along with corresponding 95% confidence

Note that if we included the parish of S. Marco above, this will instead generate Supplementary Figure S4.

```{r plot results - figure 2}
#1: sum, 2: shannonPDF, 3: shannonQuantile, 4: negentPDF, 5: uniformKL_PDF, 6: uniformKL_Quantile

# ----

# Initialize dataframe with 2.5th percentile value, 97.5th percentile value, and original value of shannonQuantile
ent_plot_df_cumq <-
  as.data.frame(
    cbind(
      stats_of_whole_boot_cumulative_50_2$b1[[3]],
      stats_of_whole_boot_cumulative_50_2$b2[[3]],
      stats_of_whole_cumulative_50_2$shannonQuantile,
      eff_number_cumulative
    )
  )
colnames(ent_plot_df_cumq) <- c("b1", "b2", "observed", "eff")

ent_plot_cumq <- ggplot(data = ent_plot_df_cumq, aes(x = filled$Date, y = observed)) +
  geom_line() +
  #geom_line(aes(y=rep(log(ncol(filled_modified[,-1])),length(filled$Date))),linetype="dashed")+
  geom_line(aes(y = rep(log(
    ncol(filled_modified[, -1])
  ), length(filled$Date))), col = "red") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = b1, ymax = b2), alpha = 0.5) +
  #geom_line(aes(y=log(eff)),col="red")+
  # coord_cartesian(ylim=c(3.5,3.95))+ #S. Marco
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(3.5, 3.9)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "12 months", date_labels = "%m-%Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Entropy (nats)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis( #create second y-axis for effective number of parishes
      trans =  ~ .,
      name = "Effective number of parishes",
      labels = function(x)
        scales::comma(round(exp(x)), accuracy = 1)
    )
  ) +
  labs(y = "Entropy (nats)", x = "Date", title = "Entropy") +
  plot_theme()

# Initialize dataframe with 2.5th percentile value, 97.5th percentile value, and original value of uniformKL_Quantile

  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.35)) +
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.5))+ #S. Marco

  labs(y = "Negentropy (nats)", x = "Date", title = "Negentropy") +
```

```{r plot results - supplementary figure s2}
#1: sum, 2: shannonPDF, 3: shannonQuantile, 4: negentPDF, 5: uniformKL_PDF, 6: uniformKL_Quantile
#can plot against incidence ("sum") if you want

colnames(ent_plot_df_instq) <- c("b1", "b2", "observed", "nonzeroes")

ent_plot_instq <- ggplot(data = ent_plot_df_instq, aes(x = filled$Date, y = observed)) +
```

## Figure 4

Fifth, we create Figure 4, a plot of Shannon entropy of the quantile functions for each sestiere's cumulative mortality data along with the 95% confidence intervals generated from bootstrapping.

```{r plot results - figure 4}
#----
# Documentation: Figure 4
# Goal: Time series plot of shannonQuantile of each sestiere, differentiated via colors
# ----

stat_of_interest <-
  3 #1: sum, 2: shannonPDF, 3: shannonQuantile, 4: negentPDF, 5: uniformKL_PDF, 6: uniformKL_Quantile
b1_plot_mat <-
  matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(filled_modified), ncol = 6) #6 = number of stats, not sestieri
b2_plot_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(filled_modified), ncol = 6)
observed_plot_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(filled_modified), ncol = 6)

for (i in 1:6) { #6 = number of sestieri
  b1_plot_mat[, i] <-
    stats_by_sestiere_boot_cumulative_50_2[[i]]$b1[, stat_of_interest]
  b2_plot_mat[, i] <-
    stats_by_sestiere_boot_cumulative_50_2[[i]]$b2[, stat_of_interest]
  observed_plot_mat[, i] <-
    stats_by_sestiere_cumulative_50_2[[i]][[stat_of_interest]]
}

time_series <- 1:nrow(filled_modified)
series_names <- unique(sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere)

# Ensure matrices are data.frames
lower_df <- as.data.frame(b1_plot_mat)
upper_df <- as.data.frame(b2_plot_mat)
observed_df <- as.data.frame(observed_plot_mat)

# Add time column
lower_df$time <- upper_df$time <- observed_df$time <- time_series

# Pivot longer
lower_long <-
  pivot_longer(lower_df,-time, names_to = "series", values_to = "lower")
upper_long <-
  pivot_longer(upper_df,-time, names_to = "series", values_to = "upper")
obs_long   <-
  pivot_longer(observed_df,-time, names_to = "series", values_to = "observed")

# Combine all into one long dataframe
plot_df <- lower_long %>%
  left_join(upper_long, by = c("time", "series")) %>%
  left_join(obs_long, by = c("time", "series")) %>%
  mutate(series = factor(series, levels = paste0("V", 1:6), labels = series_names))

# Calculate the maximum possible entropy for each sestiere
maxima_vec <- rep(0, length(unique(sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere)))
for (s in unique(sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere)) {
  maxima_vec[match(s, unique(sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere))] <-
    log(length(sestiere_df_modified$Parish[sestiere_df_modified$Sestiere ==
                                             s]))
}

# Add these maxima values as a column in the plot dataframe
maxima_column <- rep(maxima_vec, nrow(filled_modified))
plot_df$maxima <- maxima_column
```

## Figure 1

The goal with Figure 1 is to illustrate how the distribution of disease evolves over the course of the epidemic. Given cumulative mortality data, we represent the distribution of disease in 3 ways: a choropleth map, a quantile function, and a PDF. We then isolate 3 time points corresponding to the start, peak, and end of the epidemic. Finally, we graph these representations at every time point, producing a 3x3 grid.

### Choropleth Maps

The goal of this section is to generate both the choropleth maps as described above for Figure 1 as well as a GIF that cycles through the choropleth map at the end of every month (Supplementary Video S1).

The following code is a modification of G. Lazzari and G. Colavizza's notebook titled "Venice deaths on Maps" published in their 2020 paper. The previous code uses some packages that are no longer supported, so some modifications are made in this notebook.

```{r choropleth load packages}
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringi)
library(readr)
library(viridisLite)
```

#### Prepare spatial object

```{r choropleth load shap file}
parish_key <- function(x) {
  x <- stringi::stri_trans_general(x, id = "Latin-ASCII")
  x <- tolower(x)
  gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "", x)
}

shape_sf <- st_read(
  "1729_PAR_CONF.shp",
  quiet = TRUE
) |>
  transmute(
    parish_map = NAME,
    parish_key = parish_key(NAME)
  ) |>
  st_make_valid()

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(shape_sf$parish_key))
```

#### Original deaths on map

Load clean dataset

```{r choropleth load clean dataset}
filled_for_map <- filled_modified

names(filled_for_map)[1] <- "Date"
filled_for_map$Date <- as.Date(filled$Date)

mortality_long <- filled_for_map |>
  mutate(day_index = seq_len(nrow(filled_for_map))) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(Date, day_index),
    names_to = "parish_data",
    values_to = "daily_deaths"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    parish_key = parish_key(parish_data),
    daily_deaths = replace_na(as.numeric(daily_deaths), 0)
  ) |>
  arrange(parish_key, day_index) |>
  group_by(parish_key) |>
  mutate(
    cumulative_deaths = cumsum(daily_deaths)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

Prepare population table

```{r prepare population table}
population_key <- population_specified_modified |>
  transmute(
    parish_data = Parish,
    parish_key = parish_key(Parish),
    population_people = Population * 1000
  )

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(population_key$parish_key))
```

Join population and calculate what is mapped

```{r join population}
map_values <- mortality_long |>
  left_join(
    population_key,
    by = "parish_key",
    suffix = c("", "_population")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    cumulative_mortality =
      cumulative_deaths / population_people
  )
```

Check the join

```{r check join}
unmatched_shape_names <- shape_sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  anti_join(
    distinct(map_values, parish_key),
    by = "parish_key"
  )

unmatched_data_names <- map_values |>
  distinct(parish_key, parish_data) |>
  anti_join(
    st_drop_geometry(shape_sf),
    by = "parish_key"
  )

print(unmatched_shape_names)
print(unmatched_data_names)
```
Specify which days we want to investigate:

```{r specify days of interest}
end_of_month_indices <- c(which(day(filled$Date) == 1)[-1] - 1, nrow(filled_modified))
days_vec <- c(7, end_of_month_indices[22], end_of_month_indices[36])
```

Create map objects:

```{r create map objects}
map_sf_list <- lapply(days_vec, function(selected_day) {
  values_for_day <- map_values |>
    filter(day_index == selected_day)

  shape_sf |>
    left_join(values_for_day, by = "parish_key")
})
```

Save the data.

```{r save choropleth data}
figure1_map_source <- map_values |>
  filter(day_index %in% days_vec) |>
  select(
    date = Date,
    parish = parish_data,
    population_people,
    daily_deaths,
    cumulative_deaths,
    cumulative_mortality
  )
```

Set up the legend and color scale.

```{r plot choropleths}
tmap_mode("plot")

map_breaks <- seq(0, 0.7, by = 0.1)
map_labels <- sprintf(
  "%.1f-%.1f",
  head(map_breaks, -1),
  tail(map_breaks, -1)
)

map_colors <- viridisLite::viridis(
  n = length(map_labels),
  option = "D",
  begin = 0.05,
  end = 0.95
)

mortality_scale <- function() {
  tm_scale_intervals(
    style = "fixed",
    breaks = map_breaks,
    labels = map_labels,
    values = map_colors,
    value.na = "#BDBDBD",
    label.na = "Missing"
  )
}
```

Create the plots without individual legends.

```{r create individual choropleths}
make_map_panel <- function(map_data) {
  tm_shape(map_data) +
    tm_polygons(
      fill = "cumulative_mortality",
      fill.scale = mortality_scale(),
      fill.legend = tm_legend_hide(),
      col = "white",
      lwd = 0.4
    ) +
    tm_layout(
      frame = FALSE,
      bg.color = "white",
      text.fontfamily = "Helvetica",

      # Add internal room around the map
      inner.margins = c(0.04, 0.04, 0.04, 0.04),
      outer.margins = c(0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01)
    )
}

map_tm_list <- lapply(map_sf_list, make_map_panel)
map_grob_list <- lapply(map_tm_list, tmap_grob)

make_map <- function(map_data) {
  tm_shape(map_data) +
    tm_polygons(
      fill = "cumulative_mortality",
      col = "white",
      lwd = 0.4,
      fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(
        style = "fixed",
```

### PDF and Quantile Graphs

In this section, we will generate the PDF and Quantile Graphs included in Figure 1. For the quantile function and PDF graphs, we overlay the corresponding maximum entropy distribution in red.

First, we define our functions.

```{r PDF_and_Quantile_graphs}
# Find the indices in filled$Date of the last day of every month
end_of_month_indices <- c(which(day(filled$Date) == 1)[-1] - 1, nrow(filled_modified))

# Create a new negent function that provides debugging information when NAs are present
negent_new <- function (x, K = ceiling(log2(length(x))) + 1){ # K = number of bins
  p <- table(cut(x, breaks = K))/length(x)
  bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = K + 1)
  bins2 <- rep(0, K)
  for(i in 1:K){
    bins2[i] <- (bins[i] + bins[i+1]) / 2
  }
  y <- dnorm(bins2, mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x))
  y <- y / sum(y)
  if(length(which(is.na(y))) == K){
    y <- rep(0, K)
  }
  if(length(as.numeric(p)) != length(y)){
    print("Something went wrong")
    print(paste("p", length(as.numeric(p))))
    print(as.numeric(p))
    print(paste("y", length(y)))
    print(y)
  } else if(anyNA(as.numeric(p))){
    print(paste("p had an NA", as.numeric(p)))
  } else if(anyNA(y)){
    print(paste("y had an NA", y))
  }
  return(KL_new(as.numeric(p), y))
}

# Create a modified PDF approximation function that adds a small epsilon to avoid NAs
PDF_approx_new <- function (x, K = ceiling(log2(length(x))) + 1, epsilon = 1e-05){
  p <- table(cut(x+epsilon, breaks = K))/length(x)
  return(p)
}
```

While we use histogram approximation of the PDF with bin number determined by Sturges' rule in the analysis, for the purposes of illustration we use an Epanechnikov kernel with 512 bins in this figure.

```{r PDF_epanechnikov}
# Define the PDF approximation function using an Epanechnikov kernel of 512 bins
PDF_approx_epanechnikov <- function (cv){
  #kern <- density(cv,n=512,from=0,to=max(cv),kernel="epanechnikov",bw="bcv")$y
  kern <- density(cv, n = 512, from = min(cv), to = max(cv), bw = "nrd0")$y
  kern <- kern / sum(kern)
  return(kern)
}
```

Next, we define the function that generates the histogram-approximated normal distribution with the same mean and variance as the data.

```{r define normal_approx}
#----
#' Documentation: normal_approx
#' Usage: normal_approx(x, K)
#' @description: Takes in a vector of mortality at a given time point and generates a histogram approximation of a Gaussian distribution with identical mean and variance to the data

#' Arguments/Options:
#' @param x: a vector containing the mortality rates of each parish at a specific point in time
#' @param K: the number of bins to use (DEFAULT: ceiling(log2(length(x))) + 1), Sturges' Rule)

#' @return: a vector of length K containing the densities in each bin of the normal distribution as described above
#----
normal_approx <- function (x, K = ceiling(log2(length(x))) + 1){
  bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = K + 1)
  bins2 <- rep(0, K)
  for(i in 1:K){
    bins2[i] <- (bins[i] + bins[i + 1]) / 2
  }
  y <- dnorm(bins2, mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x))
  y <- y / sum(y)
  return(y)
}
```

Identify the bootstrapped 95% CIs for the coefficient of variation.

```{r bootstrapped coefficient of variation}
# Initialize matrix to calculate coefficient of variation and 95% CI using 999 resamplings
coeff_var_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = 999, ncol = 3)

for(i in 1:999) {
  indices <- sample(1:ncol(filled_modified[,-1]), replace = TRUE)
  booted_data <- filled_modified[,-1][, indices]
  pop_spec <- population_specified_modified[indices, ]
  for (j in days_vec) {
    day <- j
    case_vec <-
      as.numeric(colSums(booted_data[1:day, ])) / (pop_spec$Population * 1000)
    var_mean <- sd(case_vec) / mean(case_vec)
    coeff_var_mat[i, match(j, days_vec)] <- var_mean
  }
}
sort(coeff_var_mat[,1], decreasing = FALSE)[25] #January 7, 1629 low
sort(coeff_var_mat[,1], decreasing = FALSE)[975] #January 7, 1629 high
sort(coeff_var_mat[,2], decreasing = FALSE)[25] #December 31, 1631 low
sort(coeff_var_mat[,2], decreasing = FALSE)[975] #December 31, 1631 high
sort(coeff_var_mat[,3], decreasing = FALSE)[25] #October 31, 1630 low
sort(coeff_var_mat[,3], decreasing = FALSE)[975] #October 31, 1630 high
```

Produce the graphs for the PDF and inverse CDF.

```{r produce pdf and quantile graphs}
quantile_source_list <- vector("list", length(days_vec))
pdf_source_list <- vector("list", length(days_vec))

for(i in days_vec){
  day <- i
  case_vec <- as.numeric(colSums(filled_modified[1:day,-1])) / (population_specified_modified$Population * 1000)
  instantaneous_case_vec <- as.numeric(filled_modified[day, -1]) / (population_specified_modified$Population * 1000)
  var_mean <- sd(case_vec) / mean(case_vec)
  print(var_mean)
  case_vec_norm <- case_vec / sum(case_vec)
  q_func <- sort(case_vec_norm)
  pdf_vec <- as.numeric(PDF_approx_new(case_vec))
  normal <- normal_approx(case_vec)
  shannon_normal[match(i, days_vec)] <- -1 * sum(normal[normal != 0] * log(normal[normal != 0]))
  
  # plot(pdf_vec,main=paste(filled$Date[day],round(var_mean,3))) # PDF
  # lines(normal_approx(case_vec),col="red")
  # barplot(q_func) #quantile
  # plot(PDF_approx_epanechnikov(case_vec))
  
  new_negent[match(i, days_vec)] <- negent_new(case_vec)
  old_negent[match(i, days_vec)] <- negent(case_vec)
  max_ent_uniform <- rep(1/length(case_vec_norm), length(case_vec_norm))
  q_func_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(q_func,max_ent_uniform))
  
  # Generate quantile function graphs 
  
  # Increase y limits for graph from January 7, 1629 since the small number of total cases leads to large proportions in individual parishes
  if(match(i, days_vec) == 1) {
    quantile_graph <-
      ggplot(data = q_func_df, aes(y = q_func, x = seq(1, ncol(filled_modified[, -1])))) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
      geom_bar(
        aes(y = max_ent_uniform),
        stat = "identity",
        fill = "red",
        alpha = 0.25
      ) +
      labs(y = "Normalized mortality", x = "Parishes ranked by mortality") +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.15)) +
      plot_theme()
    # Only title the first graph to avoid redundancy
    quantile_graph <- quantile_graph + ggtitle("Inverse CDF")
  } else {
    quantile_graph <-
      ggplot(data = q_func_df, aes(y = q_func, x = seq(1, ncol(filled_modified[, -1])))) +
      geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
      geom_bar(
        aes(y = max_ent_uniform),
        stat = "identity",
        fill = "red",
        alpha = 0.25
      ) +
      labs(y = "Normalized mortality", x = "Parishes ranked by mortality") +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.04)) +
      plot_theme()
  }
  
  # Generate PDF graphs
  
  K <- ceiling(log2(length(case_vec))) + 1
  bins <- seq(min(case_vec), max(case_vec), length.out = K + 1)
  bins2 <- rep(0, K)
  for(j in 1:K){
    bins2[j] <- (bins[j] + bins[j+1]) / 2
  }
  bins3 <- seq(from = min(case_vec), to = max(case_vec), length.out = 512)
  pdf_vec_2 <- PDF_approx_epanechnikov(case_vec)
  max_ent_normal <- dnorm(bins3, mean = mean(case_vec), sd = sd(case_vec))
  max_ent_normal <- max_ent_normal / sum(max_ent_normal)
  pdf_df <- data.frame(x = bins3, y = pdf_vec_2, y2 = max_ent_normal)
  
  # Increase y limits for the graph on January 7, 1629 for the same reason as before
  if(match(i, days_vec) == 1) {
    PDF_graph <- ggplot(data = pdf_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
      geom_density(
        stat = "identity",
        fill = "darkgrey",
        alpha = 0.5,
        lwd = 0.25
      ) +
      geom_density(
        aes(y = y2),
        stat = "identity",
        fill = "red",
        alpha = 0.25,
        lwd = 0.25
      ) +
      labs(y = "Normalized parish count", x = "Cumulative mortality") +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.01)) +
      plot_theme()
    # Only title the first graph to avoid redundancy
    PDF_graph <- PDF_graph + ggtitle("PDF")
  } else {
    PDF_graph <- ggplot(data = pdf_df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
      geom_density(
        stat = "identity",
        fill = "darkgrey",
        alpha = 0.5,
        lwd = 0.25
      ) +
      geom_density(
        aes(y = y2),
        stat = "identity",
        fill = "red",
        alpha = 0.25,
        lwd = 0.25
      ) +
      labs(y = "Normalized parish count", x = "Cumulative mortality") +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.006)) +
      plot_theme()
  }
  quantile_graph_list[[match(i, days_vec)]] <- quantile_graph

  PDF_graph_list[[match(i, days_vec)]] <- PDF_graph
  
  PDF_and_quantile_graph <- plot_grid(plotlist = list(PDF_graph,quantile_graph))
  
  # Save data for quantile function and PDF graphs
  m <- match(i, days_vec)

  quantile_source_list[[m]] <- data.frame(
    panel = "b",
    date = filled$Date[day],
    data_type = "quantile",
    parish = NA_character_,
    rank = seq_along(q_func),
    x = NA_real_,
    observed = q_func,
    reference = max_ent_uniform
  )
  
  pdf_source_list[[m]] <- data.frame(
    panel = "c",
    date = filled$Date[day],
    data_type = "PDF",
    parish = NA_character_,
    rank = NA_integer_,
    x = bins3,
    observed = pdf_vec_2,
    reference = max_ent_normal
  )
}
```

```{r save figure 1 data}
# Convert historical dates to text for correct Excel rendering
historical_date_text <- function(x, style = "long") {
  if (!inherits(x, "Date")) {
    x <- as.Date(x, origin = "1970-01-01")
  }

  if (style == "numeric") {
    return(format(x, "%m-%d-%Y"))
  }

  sub(
    " 0",
    " ",
    format(x, "%B %d, %Y"),
    fixed = TRUE
  )
}

write_figure1_section <- function(
    wb,
    sheet,
    title,
    data,
    start_row,
    table_name
) {

  number_of_columns <- ncol(data)

  # Write the standalone panel heading
  writeData(
    wb,
    sheet = sheet,
    x = title,
    startRow = start_row,
    startCol = 1,
    colNames = FALSE
  )

  # Apply section styling across the width of the table
  addStyle(
    wb,
    sheet = sheet,
    style = section_style,
    rows = start_row,
    cols = seq_len(number_of_columns),
    gridExpand = TRUE,
    stack = TRUE
  )

  # Merge the section-heading cells
  mergeCells(
    wb,
    sheet = sheet,
    rows = start_row,
    cols = seq_len(number_of_columns)
  )

  setRowHeights(
    wb,
    sheet = sheet,
    rows = start_row,
    heights = 20
  )

  # Write the actual Excel table
  writeDataTable(
    wb,
    sheet = sheet,
    x = data,
    startRow = start_row + 1,
    startCol = 1,
    tableName = table_name,
    tableStyle = "TableStyleMedium2",
    headerStyle = header_style,
    withFilter = TRUE
  )

  # Return the starting row for the next section
  start_row + nrow(data) + 4
}
```

# Sensitivity Analyses

In this section, we conduct several sensitivity analyses to address the extent to which the limitations of our methodology may have affected our results.

## Testing Binning Methods

In this section, we compare the entropy of the PDF with that of the histogram-approximated normal distribution with identical mean and variance to the data. In particular, we make this comparison for three bin selection methods.

### Sturges' Rule

Here, we implement Sturges' Rule to determine the number of bins ($K = \lceil \log_2(n)\rceil + 1$). Since we have a consistent number of parishes ($n = 50$), Sturges' Rule will always result in a 7 bin histogram. 

```{r find PDF max entropy Sturges rule}
normal_approx <- function (x, K = ceiling(log2(length(x))) + 1){
  bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = K + 1)
  bins2 <- rep(0, K)
  for(i in 1:K){
    bins2[i] <- (bins[i] + bins[i + 1]) / 2
  }
  y <- dnorm(bins2, mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x))
  y <- y / sum(y)
  y_2 <- diff(pnorm(bins, mean(x), sd(x)))
  return(y)
  #return(log(2 * pi * exp(1)*sigma2)*1/2 + sum(p * log(p)))
}

SR_shannon_PDF_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))
SR_max_entropy_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))
max_differential_entropy_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))
msos_negent_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))
KL_divergence_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))
KL_function_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))
case_df <- as.data.frame(matrix(data = NA, nrow = nrow(filled_modified), ncol = ncol(filled_modified[,-1])))

for(i in 1:nrow(filled_modified)){
  case_vector_2 <- colSums(filled_modified[1:i,-1])/(population_specified_modified$Population * 1000)
  case_df[i,] <- case_vector_2
  p <- normal_approx(case_vector_2)
  max_entropy <- -1 * sum(p*log(p))
  max_differential_entropy <- log(sd(case_vector_2) * sqrt(2 * pi * exp(1))) #Differential Entropy
  kern <- as.numeric(PDF_approx(case_vector_2))
  kern <- kern/sum(kern)
  
  shannon_PDF <- -1 * sum(kern[kern != 0] * log(kern[kern != 0]))
  
  KL_divergence <- (-1 * shannon_PDF) - sum(kern[kern != 0] * log(p[kern != 0]))
  
  KL_function <- KL_new(kern, p)
  
  SR_shannon_PDF_vec[i] <- shannon_PDF
  SR_max_entropy_vec[i] <- max_entropy
  KL_divergence_vec[i] <- KL_divergence
  KL_function_vec[i] <- KL_function
  max_differential_entropy_vec[i] <- max_differential_entropy
  msos_negent_vec[i] <- negent(case_vector_2)
}
```

Now, we plot:

1. the entropy of the resulting PDF (black) against that of the normal distribution with the same mean and variance (red) for every day in the epidemic
2. the negentropy of the PDF, calculated as entropy of the normal distribution - entropy of the PDF

#### Compare Negentropy Calculations

Compare multiple calculations for negentropy using Sturges' Rule:

1. Black - Subtracting entropy of histogram-approximated normal by entropy of histogram-approximated PDF
2. Blue - KL divergence of histogram-approximated PDF $P(x)$ from histogram-approximated normal $Q(x)$ using the calculation $-H(P(x)) + H(P(x), Q(x))$ where $H(P(x), Q(x))$ is the cross entropy, defined as $H(P(x), Q(x)) = -\sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} p(x)\log q(x)$
3. Orange - Negentropy estimates obtained from the msos package's negent function, which calculates negentropy as $h(Y_G)-H(Y)$ where $h(Y_G)$ is the differential entropy of the normal distribution with the same mean and variance as the data (defined as $\frac{1}{2} \log \left( 2 \pi e \cdot \sigma^2 \right)$) and $H(Y)$ is the entropy (not differential entropy) of the histogram-approximated PDF
4. Pink - KL divergence of histogram-approximated PDF $P(x)$ from histogram-approximated normal $Q(x)$ using the KL_new function defined earlier in this notebook.

```{r compare negentropy calculations}
SR_plot_df %>% ggplot(aes(x = filled$Date, y = SR_max_entropy_vec - SR_shannon_PDF_vec)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(x = filled$Date, y = KL_divergence_vec), color = "blue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = filled$Date, y = msos_negent_vec), color = "orange", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(x = filled$Date, y = KL_function_vec), color = "pink", alpha = 0.5) + #nearly identical to KL_divergence_vec
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.05, 0.5)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "12 months", date_labels = "%m-%Y") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(y = "Negentropy (nats)", x = "Date", title = "Negentropy")
```

All of these graphs appear to be vertical shifts of one another, confirming that they represent the same underlying statistic. For the purposes of consistency, we use the msos negent function.

### Freedman-Diaconis

Here, we implement the Freedman-Diaconis rule to determine our bin width. The Freedman-Diaconis rule states that $\text{Bin width} = 2 \cdot \frac{\text{IQR}(x)}{\sqrt[3]{x}}$. 

```{r find PDF max entropy using freedman diaconis}
freedman_diaconis <- function (x){
  bin_width = 2 * IQR(x) * (length(x))^(-1/3)
  num_bins = ceiling((max(x) - min(x))/bin_width)
  return(num_bins)
}

FD_max_entropy_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))
FD_max_differential_entropy_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))
FD_shannon_PDF_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))

# Exclude the first day since the high prevalence of zeroes results in undefined IQR
for(i in 2:nrow(filled_modified)){
  case_vector_2 <- colSums(filled_modified[1:i,-1])/(population_specified_modified$Population * 1000)
  num_bins <- as.numeric(freedman_diaconis(case_vector_2))
  p <- normal_approx(case_vector_2, K = num_bins)
  max_entropy <- -1 * sum(p*log(p))
  max_differential_entropy <- log(sd(case_vector_2) * sqrt(2 * pi * exp(1))) #Differential Entropy
  kern <- as.numeric(PDF_approx(case_vector_2, K = num_bins))
  kern <- kern/sum(kern)
  shannon_PDF <- -1 * sum(kern[kern != 0] * log(kern[kern != 0]))
  
  FD_max_entropy_vec[i] <- max_entropy
  FD_max_differential_entropy_vec[i] <- max_differential_entropy
  FD_shannon_PDF_vec[i] <- shannon_PDF
}

```

### Kernel-Density Estimation

Finally, here we use Kernel-Density Estimation (KDE) with 512 bins. Note that because we are using KDE to approximate differential entropy, the entropy values may be negative. However, because these differential entropy estimates are being compared against the differential entropy of the normal distribution, the negentropy values should still be similar to those obtained from the other two binning methods. 

```{r kde entropy}
kde_entropy <- function(x, n_points = 512) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]

  if (length(x) < 2L || length(unique(x)) < 2L) {
    return(c(entropy = NA_real_,
             maximum_entropy = NA_real_,
             negentropy = NA_real_))
  }

  d <- density(x, n = n_points)
  dx <- d$x[2L] - d$x[1L]

  f <- d$y / sum(d$y * dx)
  positive <- f > 0

  h <- -sum(f[positive] * log(f[positive])) * dx

  mu <- sum(d$x * f) * dx
  variance <- sum((d$x - mu)^2 * f) * dx
  h_normal <- 0.5 * log(2 * pi * exp(1) * variance)

  c(
    entropy = h,
    maximum_entropy = h_normal,
    negentropy = h_normal - h
  )
}

KDE_max_entropy_vec <- rep(0, nrow(filled_modified))
KDE_shannon_PDF_vec <- rep(0, nrow(filled_modified))

for (i in 1:nrow(filled_modified)) {
  case_vector_2 <- colSums(filled_modified[1:i, -1]) / (population_specified_modified$Population * 1000)
  kde_output_vec <- kde_entropy(case_vector_2)
  KDE_shannon_PDF_vec[i] <- kde_output_vec[1]
  KDE_max_entropy_vec[i] <- kde_output_vec[2]
}
```

## Dynamic Parish Populations

In this section, we repeat our entropy calculations using dynamic parish populations; specifically, the population of a parish on day $d$ is represented as the population of that parish on January 1, 1629 minus the total deaths in that parish up to but not including day $d$. Ignoring births, the purpose of this analysis is to quantify the extent to which the assumption of fixed parish populations artifactually drives the distribution of cumulative mortality towards uniformity. We also test how the effect of this modification changes when we begin our analysis on January 1, 1629 vs. when we begin our analysis on the first day of the outbreak. 

Identify the first day of the outbreak (new_start_date).

```{r start on outbreak}
# Find how many parishes had zero deaths on a particular day
num_zeroes <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(filled_modified))

for(i in 1:nrow(filled_modified)){
  num_zeroes[i] <- sum(filled_modified[i,-1] == 0)
}

# Print the day on which the number of parishes with at least one death was greatest
print(match(min(num_zeroes), num_zeroes))

# Print the index of September 1, 1630
print(match(as.Date("1630-09-01", format = "%Y-%m-%d"), filled_modified$Date))

# After manually going through the data, day 637 is when the number of deaths rises above the levels reached in the secondary wave.
new_start_date <- 1 #Set this as 1 if we want to start on January 1, 1629
```

To distinguish between entropy increasing due to the first instance of a case in a parish and the overall distribution approaching uniformity, we identify the first day after our new start date that all parishes have at least one case.

```{r find first day with all non-zero parishes}
non_zero_parish_day <- NA_real_
```

If we're starting at the epidemic, remove all of the parishes that don't have any cases 30 days after the start of the epidemic to eliminate the possibility that entropy increases simply because parishes with zero cases get their first case.

```{r new filled_modified}

  outliers_temporary <- c("S.Polo", "S.Stae", "S.Marco", "S.Basso", "S.Pantalon", "S.Silvestro", "S.Simon.Grande", "S.Toma", "S.Severo")
  filled_modified_temporary <- filled[, !(colnames(filled) %in% outliers_temporary)]
  population_specified_modified_temporary <- population_specified[!(population_specified$Parish %in% outliers_temporary),]
} else {
  filled_modified_temporary <- filled_modified
  population_specified_modified_temporary <- population_specified_modified
}
```

Define function to compare dynamic and non-dynamic parish populations.

```{r non-dynamic parish populations}
dynamic_population_comparison <-
  function(death_data,
           population_data,
           start_date,
           dynamic = FALSE) {
    
    instantaneous_mortality_df <-
      as.data.frame(matrix(
        NA_real_,
        nrow = nrow(death_data),
        ncol = ncol(death_data) - 1
      ))
    
    population_data_copy <- population_data
    
    shannonPDF_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(death_data))
    shannonNormal_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(death_data))
    shannonQuantile_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(death_data))
    negentPDF_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(death_data))
    uniformKL_Quantile_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(death_data))
    
    for (i in start_date:nrow(death_data)) {
      instantaneous_cv <-
        death_data[i,-1] / (population_data_copy$Population * 1000)
      instantaneous_mortality_df[i,] <- instantaneous_cv
      
      cumulative_cv <-
        colSums(instantaneous_mortality_df[start_date:i, ])
      cumulative_cv <- sort(cumulative_cv)
      
      # Normalized case vector (cumulative_cv_norm): quantile function
      cumulative_cv_norm <- cumulative_cv / sum(cumulative_cv)
      
      histogram_normal <- normal_approx(cumulative_cv_norm)
      histogram_normal_entropy <-
        -1 * sum(histogram_normal * log(histogram_normal))
      
      kern <- PDF_approx(cumulative_cv)
      kern <- kern / sum(kern)
      
      shannon_PDF <- -1 * sum(kern[kern != 0] * log(kern[kern != 0]))
      
      #kde_output_vec_2 <- kde_entropy(cumulative_cv)
      
      #differential_entropy_PDF <- kde_output_vec_2[1]
      #max_entropy_PDF <- kde_output_vec_2[2]
      
      #negent_PDF <- max_entropy_PDF - differential_entropy_PDF
      
      #negent_PDF <- negent(cumulative_cv)
      
      negent_PDF <- KL_new(kern, histogram_normal)
      
      shannon_quantile <-
        -1 * sum(cumulative_cv_norm[cumulative_cv_norm != 0] * log(cumulative_cv_norm[cumulative_cv_norm != 0]))
      
      uniform_KL_quantile <-
        KL_new(cumulative_cv_norm, rep(
          1 / length(cumulative_cv_norm),
          length(cumulative_cv_norm)
        ))
      
      if (dynamic) {
        population_data_copy$Population <-
          population_data_copy$Population - (as.numeric(death_data[i, -1]) / 1000)
      }
      
      shannonPDF_vec[i] <- shannon_PDF
      shannonNormal_vec[i] <- histogram_normal_entropy
      shannonQuantile_vec[i] <- shannon_quantile
      negentPDF_vec[i] <- negent_PDF
      uniformKL_Quantile_vec[i] <- uniform_KL_quantile
    }
    return(
      list(
        shannonPDF = shannonPDF_vec,
        shannonNormal = shannonNormal_vec,
        shannonQuantile = shannonQuantile_vec,
        negentPDF = negentPDF_vec,
        uniformKL_Quantile = uniformKL_Quantile_vec
      )
    )
  }
```
